messages:
ada: Nightly perf alert from the dashboard — kernel-selector p99 jumped ~28% starting ~2026-03-17 02:00 UTC on runtime-kernel-1. Looks temporally aligned with the merge of PR#4521 (batch-prefetch heuristics). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/ker-sel-p99 :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

mike: Seen it too. Canary traffic shows smaller bump but KV cache hit rate dropped ~12%. Might be eviction due to more aggressive prefetching.

jing: kicked an automated bisect (git-bisect with perf harness). Bisect narrowed to commit 9f7e6b5 from PR#4521 — change was in prefetch heuristics and the probe frequency.

ci-bot: Perf CI job #7821 failed on nightly-regression: p99 +30% vs baseline, test vector: long-concat-512/1024. Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/7821/logs

ada: Can we pause the rollout? If bisect confirms we should revert or hotfix. @mike can you gate the canary? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mike: Paused the canary rollout and set traffic holdback to 0%. Opened revert branch: https://git.redwood.internal/r/reverts/4521-revert. Will try a hotfix branch too.

jing: Quick profiling snapshot (flamegraph link: https://prof.redwood.internal/fg/216123): extra time in select_kernel_for_request() and probe_kernel_path(). Key diff in code: changed threshold from 512->256 and enabled eager_probe for seq_len >= 256. Snippet:

```
// before (PR 4500)
if (seq_len > 512) {
  probe = true; // rare
}
// after (PR 4521)
if (seq_len >= 256) {
  probe = true; // more common
}
```

jing: That change increases kernel-selection churn which breaks batching affinity; more probes -> more kernel switches -> smaller effective batches -> higher tail latency.

ada: Also seeing KV hit rate numbers: baseline kv_hit_rate=0.87 -> current kv_hit_rate=0.75 (10k-sample window). Evictions up ~18%. That matches theory: aggressive prefetch pushes out hot KV entries.

sre-bot: Runtime metrics excerpt:

"kernel_switches_per_min": "+45%",
"batch_size_p50": "-12%",
"kv_evictions_rate": "+18%",
"p99_latency_ms": "+28%"

lee: Possible mitigations: revert change OR change to soft-sampling (probabilistic probe 0.5%) OR keep threshold 512 but introduce a sampled soft-probe that doesn't evict cache entries. Can we runtime-flip the flag?

mike: I'll push a hotfix branch that sets probe_sampling = 0.005 (0.5%) and restores threshold to 512, run canary for 1 hour. Pushing now: https://git.redwood.internal/r/branches/hotfix/prefetch-hotfix-216123

ci-bot: Deploy to canary started for hotfix branch (deploy/216123-hotfix). Canary run will report in ~10m.

jing: I'll re-run the microbench harness focusing on batching affinity and KV hit rates. Early local run shows p99 restored to within 3% of baseline with sampling=0.005.

ada: Good — if canary looks stable for 1 hour we can roll forward. Also note: add a perf CI test that covers long-sequence prefetch behavior (512->1024) so this doesn't regress again.

mike: Added perf CI test and e2e check in https://git.redwood.internal/r/branches/perf-tests/prefetch-threshold.

ada: Thanks team. Filing follow-up postmortem and will annotate PR#4521 with the perf findings.

jing: Filing the bisect results and flamegraphs in the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.internal/216123-prefetch-slope

mike: Leaving the rollback PR open until postmortem.

ci-bot: Canary deploy finished: metrics trending back to baseline after 25m. Will keep under observation. :white_check_mark:
